result: Let R be the explicit fixed 4x5 PPT/SN3 grid state below. For EVERY complex rank-four Bob map K:C^5->C^4 whose kernel line is in either span{|0>,|2>,|3>} or span{|0>,|2>,|4>}, the actual normalized 4x4 projection of R has Schmidt number <=2. These are two entire CP^2 kernel families, not merely open patches or two-sparse lines. The state is PPT by local congruence. This is not a theorem about all 5-to-4 kernels, arbitrary 4x4 PPT states, or an SN>=3 target witness.
source: [q]=|q><q|; A=|00>+|11>+|22>, B=|01>+|12>, D=|10>-|21>, C=|02>+|34>, E=|20>+|33>, F=|23>, G=|30>, I=|32>, H=|04>. Put R=[A]+[B]+[D]+3([C]+[E]+[F]+[G]+[I]+[H]). R/31 is PPT/SN3 by the explicit certificates in frontier-20261028-grid-state-five-projections-v1.json SHA256 9863760e2ca2331164d12e62300f3ad7db5b6a17a3ef424e360d504d541004a9, based on Krebs–Gachechiladze https://arxiv.org/html/2509.07086v1 Eq.11. No novelty or priority claim.
normal_form: For a kernel in span{|0>,|2>,|3>} with nonzero |3> coefficient, after an invertible output filter write K|j>=|j> for j=0,1,2; K|3>=v0|0>+v2|2>; K|4>=|3>, for arbitrary v0,v2 in C. Put U=|v0|^2,V=|v2|^2. Primes denote images. E'=|20>+v0|30>+v2|32>, F'=v0|20>+v2|22>, G'=|30>, I'=|32>, C'=|02>+|33>, H'=|03>. The common-kernel normal form is valid because any two surjective maps with the same kernel differ by an invertible output map, and invertible local filters preserve PPT and Schmidt number.
first_phase_certificate: Set X=E'-v0G'-v2I'=|20>, A0=1+U+V, and s=-A0*conjugate(v0)/(1+A0*U). Put W=-X+s(F'-v0X) and q_z=zA'+B'+z^2D'+z^3W for z^4=1. Each q_z has SR<=2 and their phase average is [A']+[B']+[D']+[W]. In basis (E',G',I',F'), W has coordinates t0=(-(1+s*v0),(1+s*v0)*v0,(1+s*v0)*v2,s). The remainder is 3([C']+[H']) plus the Gram 3I_4-t0*t0^* over this basis. Its combinations have Alice support only on rows2,3, and its matrix is PSD when ||t0||^2=A0/(1+A0*U)<=3. Complete written details and prior exact checks are in frontier-20261028-grid-unbounded-two-head-v1.json SHA256 67790038cc1fea96c22eef45c909a852f238132584acf21a397f42746420baa2.
second_phase_certificate: Assume v2!=0 and put Z=|22>=(F'-v0E'+v0^2 G'+v0*v2 I')/v2. For beta=1+i, delta=1-i and each z^4=1, let q_z=z(A'+Z)+beta*z^2 B'+delta*D'; also q_0=A'-Z=|00>+|11>. q_0 has rank2. The upper 3x3 determinant of q_z is (2-beta*delta)z^3=0, with zero fourth row/column, so each q_z has SR<=2. Phase averaging yields (1/2)[q_0]+(1/8)sum_(z^4=1)[q_z]=[A']+[B']+[D']+[Z]. In basis (E',G',I',F'), Z has coordinates t1=(-v0/v2,v0^2/v2,v0,1/v2). Consequently the state equals that phase average, plus 3([C']+[H']), plus the Gram 3I_4-t1*t1^* over the four Alice-rows-2,3-supported vectors. This is an SR2 decomposition whenever ||t1||^2=U+(1+U+U^2)/V<=3.
exhaustion_of_all_complex_parameters: If U>=1/3, the first Gram is PSD for all V since A0(1-3U)<=0<3. If U<1/3 and V<=1, A0(1-3U)<=(2+U)(1-3U)=2-5U-3U^2<=2<3, so the first Gram is PSD, including V=0. If U<1/3 and V>1, then U+(1+U+U^2)/V<1/3+13/9=16/9<3, so the second Gram is PSD. These cases cover every complex pair (v0,v2).
projective_boundary_and_reflection: The chart boundary has kernel coefficient of |3> zero and therefore lies in span{|0>,|2>}; every such two-sparse kernel was already proved in frontier-20261028-grid-all-two-column-compressions-v1.json SHA256 4076912f4e4197244483b47eaa7d6e5d09207386840929db1d04814332ff9406. The exact local symmetry in frontier-20261028-grid-mixed-zero-three-compressions-v1.json SHA256 25278f1e460330954c54de872f9468b880fa3f3220dbab6c15954852cb139789 maps Bob |0> to -|2>, |2> to |0>, and |3> to -|4> while preserving R, so it transfers the entire first CP^2 to span{|0>,|2>,|4>}. Both kernel-plane assertions include arbitrary phases and all rank-four output maps.
entanglement: Within the first chart, 3V<4 additionally proves entanglement by the explicit 3x3 core/rank-one-minor Cauchy argument in frontier-20261028-grid-unbounded-two-head-v1.json. Those cases have SN exactly2. No entanglement claim is made outside that sufficient range.

exact_check.observed: For five Gaussian-rational pairs (v0,v2)=(0,2),(1/2,4),(i/2,1+i),(2,1),((1+i)/4,1), checked all 3x3 minors of five phase vectors, all 256 state identities, and exact Schur pivots of the residual Gram and actual PT. At (1/2,4) first Gram norm^2=276/85>3 while second Gram norm^2=85/256<3; this is a genuine three-support case newly covered by the complementary construction. At (2,1) the second Gram is indefinite but the first certificate applies. Initial test caught an erroneous choice beta*delta=-2; it was corrected to beta*delta=+2 before the successful run. Exact finite checks support the identities only; universal coverage follows from the written algebra.

limits: The union of these CP^2 families remains a proper subset of all CP^4 kernel lines for this particular 4x5 source. No claim is made for the generic full-support complement, arbitrary 4x4 PPT states, external/formal review, or novelty.
